newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - April 18.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - April 18.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - Lumber prices held to a strong upward trend but the pace of trading slowed as the week progressed, Random Lengths said in its weekly review. By Thursday, many mills were booked through the end of the month. Shipment dates reaching into May and double-digit price gains cooled buyer enthusiasm.

Other buyers, having purchased adequate volumes to cover short-term needs, paused to digest. Brisk jobsite activity in most regions kept wood moving at a steady clip though the pipeline and producers were upbeat about near-term prospects.

Southern Pine led the gains, rising $20-30 in many areas of the South. Dealers, distribution yards and treaters scrambled for stock. Warm dry weather across most of the region alleviated concern about log supplies but growing truck and rail shortages gave traders something to fret about. Car shortages were also an issue for some Western producers and a few producers on the coast were forced to rein in order files on inability to ship.
